questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with the Separation of judiciary from executive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Article-50.____​__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy

 
 
• To separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State (Article 50).
 
• ​To promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid to the poor (Article 39 A).
 
• To organise village panchayats and endow them with the necessary powers and authority to enable them to function as units of self-government (Article 40).
 
• To secure for all citizens a uniform civil code throughout the country (Article 44).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**

 
 
• Indian Constitution borrowed the idea of directive principles of state policy from Ireland.
 
• The makers of the Constitution of India were influenced by the Irish Home Rule Movement and other national movements of Ireland. 
 
• Part IV of the Indian constitution deals with the directive principles of state policy.
 
• Directive principles of state policy(DPSP) deal with economic and cultural rights.
 
• Directive Principles of state policy(DPSP) are non-justiciable.
 
• Directive principles of state policy aimed at the establishment of the welfare state.

questions.question: ______ is the key circuit board holding the essential processing parts of a computer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Motherboard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Motherboard**: The motherboard is the main circuit board of a computer.

 
 
• It houses the **CPU, RAM, and other essential components.**
 
• It also provides the electrical connections by which the other components of the system communicate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 
 
 

 **Firmware**
 
 
Firmware is a type of software that provides control, monitoring and data manipulation of engineered products and systems.

 
It's typically stored in the read-only memory of a hardware device.

 
 
 

 **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**
 
 
The CPU is the primary component of a computer that performs most of the processing inside the computer.

 
It's often called the "brain" of the computer.

 
 
 

 **Random Access Memory (RAM)**
 
 
RAM is a type of computer memory that can be read from and written to by the processor.

 
It's a volatile memory, meaning it loses its contents when the computer is turned off or restarted.

questions.question: Which among the following is correct about Reverse Repo Rate?

options.text: Reverse Repo Rate is a state in which the Value of Money is Falling and the Prices are rising, over a period of time.
When bank deposit it's excess money in RBI then RBI provides some interest to that bank. This interest is known as Reverse Repo Rate.
When RBI provides a loan to the bank for short-term between 1 to 90 days, RBI takes some interest from the bank which is termed as Reverse Repo Rate.
When the money is borrowed or lent for more than a day up to 14 days it is called Reverse Repo Rate.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When bank deposit it's excess money in RBI then RBI provides some interest to that bank. This interest is known as Reverse Repo Rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reverse repo rate is the rate of interest at which the RBI borrows funds from other banks in the short term.
 
• This is done by RBI selling government bonds/securities to banks with the commitment to buy them back at a future date.
 
• The banks use the reverse repo facility to deposit their short-term excess funds with the RBI and earn interest on it.
 
• RBI can reduce liquidity in the banking system by increasing the rate at which it borrows from banks.
 
• Hiking reverse repo rate ends up reducing the liquidity and pushes up interest rates.
 
• An increase in the reverse repo rate means that banks earn higher returns by lending to RBI. This indicates a hike in the deposit rates.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Monetary Policy tool
 Description
 
 

 Repo Rate
 
 
 
• The (fixed) interest rate at which the Reserve Bank provides overnight liquidity to banks against the collateral of government and other approved securities under the liquidity adjustment facility (LAF).
 
 
 
 

 Reverse Repo Rate
 
 
 
• The (fixed) interest rate at which the Reserve Bank absorbs liquidity, on an overnight basis, from banks against the collateral of eligible government securities under the LAF.
 
 
 
 

 Marginal Standing Facility
 
 
 
• A facility under which scheduled commercial banks can borrow an additional amount of overnight money from the Reserve Bank by dipping into their Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) portfolio up to a limit at a penal rate of interest
 
 
 
 

 Open Market Operation
 
 
 
• It is the sale and purchase of government securities and treasury bills by the RBI 
 
 
 
 

 Statutory Liquidity Ratio
 
 
 
• ​It is the money that commercial banks need to keep with themselves in the form of cash, gold, or government-authorized securities (Bonds) before providing credit to the customers.
 
• Banks get some interest on this reserve fund.
 
• SLR is decided by the Reserve Bank of India.
 
 
 
 

 Cash Reserve Ratio
 
 
 
• It is the minimum amount of deposit that the commercial banks have to hold as reserves with the central bank. 
 
• It is in the form of cash only
 
• Bank will not get any interest on the deposit from the central bank
 
• RBI decides the CRR.
 
• CRR is maintained on a daily basis.

questions.question: The plains from Ambala to the Sunderban stretch over nearly 1800 km, but the fall in its slope is hardly ______ metres.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**300**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The fall in slope refers to the change in elevation over a given distance.
 
• In this case, the plains from **Ambala to the Sunderban stretch over nearly 1800 km.**
 
• **The phrase "fall in its slope is hardly" suggests that the change in elevation is minimal.**
 
• Therefore, we need to find the option that represents a small value for the fall in slope.
 
• **Among the given options, option 2) 300 represents the smallest value.**
 
• This implies that the change in elevation over the 1800 km stretch is only 300 meters.
 
• The small value of 300 meters indicates that the terrain between **Ambala and the Sunderban has a relatively gentle slope or gradient, as the elevation change is minimal over the given distance.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About the Sunderban:**

 
 
• The Sunderban is a vast mangrove forest located in the delta region of the G**anges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers in India and Bangladesh.**
 
• **It is one of the largest mangrove ecosystems in the world and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.**
 
• The Sunderban is famous for its rich biodiversity and is home to numerous species of plants, animals, and birds.
 
• It is particularly known for its population of** Bengal tigers, which are adapted to the mangrove environment.**
 
• The area also supports other wildlife such as **crocodiles, snakes, deer, and various bird species.**
 
• **The Sunderban plays a crucial role in maintaining the ecological balance of the region.**
 
• It acts as a natural barrier, protecting the surrounding areas from storm surges and tidal waves.
 
• The mangrove forests also serve as a nursery for many aquatic species and help in stabilizing the coastline by preventing erosion.
 
• **Tourism is an important aspect of the Sunderban, with visitors coming to explore its unique ecosystem and wildlife.**
 
• Boat safaris are a popular way to experience the mangrove forests and observe the diverse flora and fauna.
 
• Overall, the** Sunderban is not only a significant ecological hotspot but also a major tourist attraction, drawing nature enthusiasts and researchers from around the world.**

questions.question: In which of the following modes of data transmission, can the data flow in both directions but in only one direction at a time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Half Duplex__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The method of communication in which transmission can take place in both directions, but happens only in one direction at a time, is called half-duplex communication__.

 __
 
• In this mode of communication, data can be sent and received, but not at the same time.
 
• Instead, data is transmitted in one direction, then the communication channel switches to transmit data in the opposite direction.
 
• This mode of communication is commonly used in walkie-talkies, two-way radios, and some forms of computer networking.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Duplex communication is a method of communication in which data can be transmitted and received simultaneously in both directions.
 
• Simplex communication is a method of communication in which data can only be transmitted in one direction, from the sender to the receiver, and not in the opposite direction.
 
 
• In other words, in simplex communication, data can flow in only one direction along a communication channel.

questions.question: Which of the following music instruments are solid instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Ghana Vadya.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ghana Vadya or Idiophones/Solid instruments which do not require tuning- 
 
• The earliest instruments invented by man are said to be the Ghana Vadya.
 
• Once constructed, this variety of instruments does not need special tuning prior to playing.
 
• They are principally rhythmic in function and are best suited as an accompaniment to folk and tribal music and dance.
 
• E.g - Jal Tarang, Ghatam etc.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Instruments have been listed below. 

 
• Avanaddha Vadya or Membranophones/Percussion instruments -
 
 
• In the Avanaddha Vadya category of instruments, the sound is produced by striking the animal skin which has been stretched across an earthern or metal pot or a wooden barrel or frame.
 
• E.g - Tabla, Mridangam, Nagara, Damaru etc. 
 
 
 
• Sushira Vadya or Aerophones/Wind instruments -
 
 
• In the Sushira Vadya group, the sound is produced by blowing air into a hollow column.
 
• The pitch of the note is determined by controlling the air passage and the melody is played by using the fingers to open and close the instrument.
 
• E.g - Flutes, Shehnai, Nadaswaram, etc. 
 
 
 
• Tata Vadya or Chordophones/Stringed instruments - 
 
 
• ​The tata vadya is a category of instruments in which sound is produced by the vibration of a string or chord.
 
• These vibrations are caused by plucking or by bowing on the string which has been pulled taut.
 
• E.g - Veena, Sitar, Sarangi etc.

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) is the ambitious program launched by Government of India in 2018 to provide ______ access to the most vulnerable sections.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is healthcare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Aarogya Yojana from Ranchi in Jharkhand on 23rd September 2018.
 
• Over two crore__ people have availed of treatment under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana.
 
• The scheme, which is the world's largest health care program, provides a cover of up to Rs. 5 lacks per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to over 10.74 crore poor and vulnerable families.
 
• It helps to reduce hospital expenditure and mitigate financial risk.
 
• It provides cashless and paperless access to services for the beneficiaries at the point of service.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The insurance cost is shared by the center and the state mostly in the ratio of 60:40.
 
• There are about 1,400 packaged rates for various medical procedures under the scheme.
 
• These packaged rates also mention the number of average days of hospitalization for a medical procedure and supporting documents that are needed.
 
• Under no circumstances can hospitals charge the beneficiary.
 
• The scheme also has prescribed a daily limit for medical management.
 
• National Health Agency has been constituted as an autonomous entity under the Society Registration Act, 1860 for effective implementation of PMJAY in alliance with state governments.
 
• This includes the formulation of PMJAY policies, development of operational guidelines, implementation mechanisms, coordination with state governments, and monitoring and oversight of PMJAY amongst others.

questions.question: Who among the following appointed Aziz Khummar a wine distiller to high administrative post?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Muhammad Tughluq.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Muhammad Tughluq appointed Ladha and Pira, two gardeners to high administrative posts.
 
• Sultan Muhammad Tughluq appointed:
 
 
• Aziz Khummar, a wine distiller,
 
• Firuz Hajjam, a barber,
 
• Manka Tabbakh, a cook, and
 
• Two gardeners, Ladha and Pira, to high administrative posts.
 
 
 
• Ziyauddin Barani, a mid-fourteenth-century chronicler, reported their appointments as a sign of Sultan’s loss of political judgment and his incapacity to rule.
 
• Barani had criticized Muhammad Tughluq for that appointment.
 
• Tughluq's appointment reflected the socio-economic stereotypes that may have been prevalent in those times.
 
• The authors of Persian tawarikh criticized the Delhi Sultans for appointing the “low and base-born” to high offices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Allauddin Khalji

 
 
• ​Allauddin Khalji was the emperor of the Khalji dynasty.
 
• He was known to drive back the Mongols' invasion from India.
 
• Alauddin instituted a number of significant administrative changes, related to revenues, price controls, and society. 
 
• Alauddin conquered the kingdoms of Gujarat, Jaisalmer, Ranthambore, Chittor, Malwa, Siwana and Jalore. 
 
 
 
• **Jalaluddin Khalji**

 
• The founder of the Khilji dynasty was Jalal-Ud-din Firuz Khalji.
 
• He was also called “Clemency Jalal-uddin” as he followed peace and wanted to rule without violence.
 
• He appointed Ala-ud-din Khilji as the Governor of Kara. Alauddin was his son-in-law and also nephew.
 
• Jalal-ud-din was treacherously murdered by Ala-Ud-din Khilji his son-in-law.

 
• Firuz Shah Tughluq

 
• He was the third ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty after the death of Mohammad-bin Tughlaq.
 
• He imposed Jizya tax on all non-Muslims and did not even exempt Brahmins and beggers as done by his predecessors.
 
• He built Feroz Shah Kotla (Kotla means fortress), peppered Delhi with gardens, constructed canals, hunting lodges, and repaired Qutub Minar, Hauz Khas (royal tank), and Surajkund (lake of the Sun).
